chunks: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: 'Fie to a man who does not devote himself during every Friday to the matter of his religion — so that he revisits it and asks about his religion.'
And in another report: '(Fie is) to every Muslim.'

key_terms.أُفٍّ: An Arabic interjection of strong disapproval, disgust, or rebuke — 'fie', 'shame on', or 'woe to'. Used here as prophetic censure.
key_terms.جُمُعَة: Friday; also can mean 'week'. The most blessed day for Muslims, and a day associated with communal gathering and learning.
key_terms.يَتَعَاهَدُهُ: To revisit, renew, or uphold a commitment; derived from 'ahd (covenant). Implies regular review and renewal of religious practice.
key_terms.يُفَرِّغُ نَفْسَهُ: To free or empty oneself — to dedicate time and attention exclusively to something. Implies clearing one's schedule.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about devoting time to religious learning on Fridays?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmitted this prophetic tradition in which the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) condemned the neglect of regular religious learning. The hadith calls upon every believer — particularly on Fridays, the sacred day of the week — to set aside time for studying, reviewing, and asking about their religious obligations. The alternate version extends this duty universally to every Muslim, emphasizing that religious knowledge is not optional but a recurring obligation.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Fie to a man who does not free himself during every Friday for the matters of his Religion, so he pacts it and asks about his Religion’.
And in another report, ‘(Fie is) to every Muslim’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from the person who he mentioned from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“The holy Prophet has said, ‘Woe is to a man who does not save a time every Friday for learning about his religion and make a habit to ask about his religion.”
In another Hadith it says, “woe is to every such Muslim.”
